title: "After My Laughter Came Tears" and the man she lived with after her husband
summary: She sings a song that fits her life and talks about her husband's death and a long relationship with another Buddy, who died of a heart attack.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: (Piano)

Now, here's a song I like, I know somebody else wrote it, but the song fits me to a tee. See my man, my husband died, the story of it piqued me. I told people, I don't care what you've got (unintelligible).
(Singing).

"Told my friends, I didn't care, (unintelligible). "I laughed the day I saw you leave. I laughed the day I saw you leave, but after my laughter came tears. (Unintelligible). After my laughter came tears." (Unintelligible).
Very nice.
"After my Laughter Came Tears." Now, that song fits me to a tee. But I know somebody wrote it. If I tried to sing it and say I wrote it, I'd be put in jail. But the song's really my story.
It's beautiful.
I told the man, told my brothers, (unintelligible) after that man died, it liked to kill me. I'm just, you know, it's about the last two years (unintelligible).
Well, I lost plenty of men. I've lost plenty of men.
The men, the ones you lose?
Oh, it's a hard question. It's a hard question.
(Unintelligible). And I'd be getting in bed, and then after while I'd reach out and there'd be nothing but the pillows. And then you get the blues so bad. (Unintelligible).
Now, who are you talking about?
The man (unintelligible).
Your husband?
No, not my real husband. The man I had after my husband died.
Who was he? What was his name?
His name was Buddy. His name was Buddy, too (unintelligible).
I see.
(Unintelligible).
How long were you with him?
All my life (unintelligible).
Oh, you were with him long.
See, my husband died pretty soon after (unintelligible), but this man, ever since my husband been dead.
Oh, so you were with him a very long time?
All my life.
Oh, I see. Was he a musical person? Did he like to --

He -- I used to sing (unintelligible). He liked the music so well. I used to just sing and play, that would make him (unintelligible). I liked his little blues he played. I used to try to get him to play for me but he wouldn't do it. But I liked those blues he played.
He played cute old blues.
When did he die?
He died of a heart attack. He went to the bathroom --
How long ago did he die?
Five years.
Five years?
(Inaudible).
